headline: US Senator Gary Peters has introduced a bipartisan bill that would require federal agencies to tell people when AI is used to make decisions about them.
score_reason: New, but an introduced bill with no stated co-sponsor or vote date.
importance_line: Americans dealing with federal agencies could be told when AI is involved and get human review of bad decisions, but the bill is only introduced and its fate is unknown.
source: Sen. Gary Peters' office, as carried by The Alpena News
summary: The Alpena News, carrying a statement from Senator Gary Peters, reports that his Transparent Automated Governance (TAG) Act would have the Office of Management and Budget, the White House budget office, tell agencies to notify people when they deal with certain automated systems or when AI helps make a critical decision about them, and to set up human review of adverse AI decisions. It is an introduced bill only, and the statement does not name its other sponsor or say when it could be voted on.
